Jordan (FinApps): Hey team — after the v12.3 push yesterday our assistant responses are coming back much shorter and sometimes miss follow-up clarifications. Not an error or latency, just feels more 'thin'. Example attached below. request_id: rq_0a1b2c3d

Alex (Support): Sorry to hear that, Jordan. Can you paste the exact prompt and the before/after outputs you observed? Also which endpoint and model name you hit?

Jordan (FinApps): Using /v1/chat/completions, model: redwood-llm-v12.3 (we were on v12.2 before). Prompt (user):
```
User: "Explain how to revoke an OAuth token and best practices for token rotation in 3-4 bullet points."
System: "You are a concise, helpful assistant."
```
Before (v12.2):
```
- Revoke the OAuth token by calling the provider's revoke endpoint, typically POST /oauth/revoke with the token in the body.
- Ensure server-side secrets are rotated: replace client secrets, re-issue refresh tokens, and invalidate old tokens in storage.
- Use short-lived access tokens + refresh tokens to limit blast radius; enforce scopes and least privilege.
- Audit token usage and log revocation events; notify users/app owners if tokens are compromised.
```
After (v12.3):
```
- Call the provider revoke endpoint.
- Rotate secrets.
- Use short-lived tokens and audit.
```
You can see v12.3 removed clarifying detail and examples.

Alex (Support): Thanks — that delta is clear. Can you also share the actual API request (headers + params) you used and whether you used streaming or function calling? Small differences in system or temperature can change verbosity.

Jordan (FinApps): Sure — here's the curl we used (sanitized):
```bash
curl https://api.redwood.inference/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "redwood-llm-v12.3",
    "messages": [{"role":"system","content":"You are a concise, helpful assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Explain how to revoke an OAuth token and best practices for token rotation in 3-4 bullet points."}],
    "temperature": 0.2,
    "max_tokens": 180,
    "stream": false
  }'
```
request_id: rq_0a1b2c3d, region: us-west-2, time: 2026-02-15T10:12:34Z

Devon (SolutionsEng): Noted. Two quick checks: (1) system prompt is inherently concise — could interact with model changes; (2) v12.3 had an optimization patch to kernel scheduling and a reduced default decode penalty in some branches. Sam, any idea if those runtime tweaks might compress outputs?

Sam (ML): We did a rollout of a perf micro-patch to reduce burst tail latency; it included an altered top-k/top-p fallback tuning for short sequences. We expected no semantic change but small decoding hyper adjustments can change token selection distribution. Can you try the same request with temperature 0.7 and/or remove the explicit system brevity instruction? Quick A/B would help.

Jordan (FinApps): I ran a quick test:
- v12.3 (same request with temp 0.7, system prompt unchanged) produced slightly fuller output but still leaner than v12.2.
- When I removed the system prompt line entirely (no system message), v12.3 matched v12.2 verbosity more closely.

Alex (Support): That suggests an interaction between default decode tuning and system-level brevity. We'll need ML to run a canonical eval. Can you also attach the exact raw responses (full JSON) for both versions? If you can paste the response objects we can inspect stop sequences or truncation flags.

Jordan (FinApps): Pasting raw JSON now — trimmed to relevant fields:
```json
{"model":"redwood-llm-v12.3","id":"res_abc","choices":[{"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"- Call the provider revoke endpoint.\n- Rotate secrets.\n- Use short-lived tokens and audit."},"finish_reason":"stop"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":45,"completion_tokens":34}}
```
and earlier (v12.2):
```json
{"model":"redwood-llm-v12.2","id":"res_def","choices":[{"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"- Revoke the OAuth token by calling the provider's revoke endpoint, typically POST /oauth/revoke with the token in the body.\n- Ensure server-side secrets are rotated: replace client secrets, re-issue refresh tokens, and invalidate old tokens in storage.\n- Use short-lived access tokens + refresh tokens to limit blast radius; enforce scopes and least privilege.\n- Audit token usage and log revocation events; notify users/app owners if tokens are compromised."},"finish_reason":"stop"}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":45,"completion_tokens":92}}
```

Sam (ML): Thanks — the completion_tokens delta is large relative to prompt. Two things ML will check: (A) whether the v12.3 decode hyperparameters (beam/penalty/k/top-p) default fallback was accidentally tightened for low-temp requests, (B) whether any post-decoding policy filters are trimming content in the short form. I'll run a targeted evaluation across a small prompt set with and without the concise system instruction.

Maya (CustomerSuccess): Jordan, we'll keep you updated and (if helpful) spin up a pinned instance of v12.2 for your workspace while we investigate — want to avoid customer-facing regressions. Alex, can you confirm if we can pin for FinApps?

Alex (Support): Yep — we can pin v12.2 per-customer. I'll open a ticket for ops to pin model for FinApps and attach the request IDs.

deploy-bot: Model rollout event: redwood-llm-v12.3 rolled to 60% of traffic in us-west-2 at 2026-02-15T09:50:12Z (batch rollout; perf micro-patch).

Sam (ML): Timeline: I'll run diffs today, focusing on: token selection stats, top-k/top-p traces, and whether the brevity system message amplifies the effect. If we reproduce, we'll push a rollback of the specific decode tuning or add a guard in the service to preserve verbosity distribution for low-temp requests. Will report by EOD PT.

Jordan (FinApps): Appreciate it. For our use case we need the richer bullets back (customers rely on detail). Also FYI we saw similar thinning in other prompt categories (how-to, policy explanations) not just dev docs. I'll watch for the status update. :pray:

Alex (Support): Thanks Jordan — ticket created #SUP-4821. Escalating to eng-ml. We'll follow up here with findings and ETA.

Sam (ML): Quick ask: can you also run the original prompt against v12.3 with the explicit param "max_new_tokens": 150 (if your client supports) and paste the response? Helps rule out a max_tokens enforcement bug.

Jordan (FinApps): Will run that now and paste results when done.

Alex (Support): Marking this as high-priority; thanks everyone.
